text: cool now the other thing with this kinda is the placing build pieces, we use to have and just have not yet reintroduced the capability to click -> drag -> place so you could cover large areas with a floor for example or the run of it with wall pieces, currently its just single piece and slow :(
resolution: Reintroduced click→drag→place on the world editor's Place tool (the plain left drag was inert since the middle-drag orbit move, req_2704 — perfect slot). Mousedown anchors at the ground point under the cursor; dragging extends a RUN: edge kinds (walls/fences/railings/arches) lay a straight line of edge pieces along the dominant drag axis on the anchor's grid line, plate kinds rect-fill every cell between anchor and cursor; props and authored meshes stay single-placement. Each run cell resolves through the existing resolvePlacement (same snap, same host validator, same storey+terrain basing), the run stays level at the anchor's terrain height, all pieces ghost live mid-drag (re-resolved only on cell change so the validator door isn't hammered per pixel), and mouseup stamps the whole run as ONE journal entry via the new placePieces batch (single click = one-piece batch on the same door; slot-replace semantics preserved). Runs cap at 400 cells with a loud console warning. Verified headless: bundle-check clean + a v8cli geometry test (horizontal/vertical wall runs, rect fill, storey+terrain y, negative coords) ALL PASS. Pure TSX — hot reload picks it up, no rebuild needed.
